heroHeadline: GSF Full Operations Launch June 1 at 15% Strength; MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Day 23 Closed; 1.5M Displaced
heroSubtitle: On June 1, 2026, the UN-authorized Gang Suppression Force (GSF) formally launched full operations in Haiti — a mandate milestone, not a deployment milestone. The force stands at approximately 800 personnel (Chad ~400, Guatemala ~75, El Salvador ~70), representing roughly 15% of the 5,500-person authorized ceiling under UNSCR 2793. Commanded by Mongolian Major General Erdenebat Batsuuri since May 14, the advance force remains exclusively deployed in Port-au-Prince's city center corridor; Cité Soleil, Martissant, the Artibonite, Centre, and Sud-Est have zero GSF coverage. Full force strength is not expected until fall–end 2026. MSF's Cité Soleil hospital — the only health facility accessible to approximately 300,000 commune residents — enters its 23rd consecutive day of forced closure. MSF partially resumed medical activities in other Port-au-Prince neighborhoods on June 1, but the Cité Soleil facility cannot reopen while surrounded by gang-controlled territory with no security force presence. The 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan remains approximately 23% funded ($198.7M of $880M secured), and approximately 1.5 million Haitians remain internally displaced — with 600,000+ in IPC Phase 5 (Catastrophe/near-famine) conditions. The US Supreme Court ruling on Temporary Protected Status for approximately 350,000 Haitian nationals remains expected in late June–early July 2026, with the Court's conservative majority appearing to lean toward upholding the Trump administration's termination authority.
